items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I wrote the strings on “Jungleland.” ... And I met with Bruce.

ctx.x: He was writing for big bands and he was very happy doing it but he was writing for the guys he said. And then he got interested, the band leader got interested, he said, “Write some bop for us.” He said, “Naa I don’t want to.” And then he was out of work. And he thought you know I’ve been writing for the musicians, what if I wrote for the people who are buying the records. And I’m so happy to hear you say that. And I don't know if you recall but we had a phone conversation about a year ago and I saved my notes.…

Ah, yes. And you know this is the fiftieth anniversary of Bruce Springsteen’s “Born to Run” album. And I wrote the strings on “Jungleland.” And the first time I really realized that I had to wait for the song to talk to me was when I wrote that arrangement. Normally I could write an arrangement for strings, a couple hours. So I went down to my office in New Jersey, to my basement. And I said I’ve got to write two arrangements for the session tomorrow. I started at 11 o’clock and I figured I’d be writing until two…
Was it partly the lyric content that led you in the direction?
